title: THE FREQUENCY BENEATH · Forty-seven
venue: private · after a paperback found in the library's return cart · Box 26
logline: A page that is a spectrogram: time along the bottom (a week), frequency up the side, and one bright band low on the scale running the whole week without a break, with a number beside it the page draws as a shape. The vacuum cleaner's hum, the tavern's cooler, the motel's ice machine: three fainter bands above it, each one stopping at night. The bright one doesn't.

panels.composition: A hand-drawn spectrogram filling the page: a week along the bottom axis, frequency up the left, three faint horizontal bands that break at night and one bright low band running unbroken the whole width, a small numeric label beside it drawn as a shape.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a hand-drawn spectrogram filling the page with a time axis along the bottom and a frequency axis up the side, three faint horizontal bands that break at intervals and one bright low band running unbroken the whole width with a small label beside it, no words legible
image.notes: 47 Hz (Vol 6: Carla Vega's recordings; WUFR's sub-carrier). The label is a shape. The band doesn't stop at night.
